\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گرم}}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مشکل} (mushkil)}{مشکل (mushkil)}]{\ur{مشکل} (mushkil) — difficult}

\label{lesson:UR-C71-mushkil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for hot, then the Urdu for slowly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مشکل}}
\textbf{\ur{مشکل}} — \emph{mushkil} — \textquotedblleft{}difficult\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مشکل}} (\emph{mushkil}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{mushkil}, \textquotedblleft{}difficult, doubtful\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{sh-k-l} (Lane). The same root gives \emph{shakl}, \textquotedblleft{}shape\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مہنگا} (mahãgā)}{مہنگا (mahãgā)}]{\ur{مہنگا} (mahãgā) — expensive}

\label{lesson:UR-C71-mahaga}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for slowly, then the Urdu for difficult.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مہنگا}}
\textbf{\ur{مہنگا}} — \emph{mahãgā} — \textquotedblleft{}expensive\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مہنگا}} (\emph{mahãgā}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{mahārgha}, \textquotedblleft{}high-priced\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9954). It is built from \emph{mahā}, \textquotedblleft{}great\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{argha}, \textquotedblleft{}price\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
